requirements.text: The system must provide an electronic method to create, amend and delete ISINs for electronically issued money market instruments.
The system must use SWIFT (ISO15022 standards) as the communication protocol.
The system must use MT 598 User Defined SWIFT messages as the format for messages.
The system must provide ISINs automatically in response to an electronic request (SWIFT).
The system must use an ISIN prefix of ZAM for money market instruments.
The system must use a new branch code “ISN” as an extension of the JSE’s current BIC address (i.e. XJSEZAJJXISN).
The system must provide 9 specific SWIFT message types for ISIN issuance, cancellation, and deregistration.
The system must include a screen for Clearing & Settlement to input manual ISINs on BCP.
The system must include a screen to update issuer codes.
The system must include a screen reflecting rejections from the JSE to STRATE for the previous day.
The system must include a screen reflecting rejections from STRATE to the JSE for the previous day.
The system must send an email to Clearing & Settlement at the time of rejection.
The system must provide a screen to look up details for a specific ISIN.
The BCP interface must enforce multi-factor authentication, dual-control (maker-checker) authorization for all manual ISIN entries, and comprehensive audit logging of all manual modifications.

Access to view and print ISIN data must be restricted via Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) based on the principle of least privilege, ensuring only authorized personnel can access specific issuer or instrument data.
The system must process and respond to an ISIN issuance request within 5 seconds of receipt.
The system must have an RTO of less than 1 hour and an RPO of 0 (no data loss) in the event of a primary site failure.
The system must process and respond to an ISIN issuance request within 5 seconds of receipt.
The system must dispatch rejection emails within 60 seconds of the rejection event occurring in the system.

OPEN: The requirement for email notifications upon rejection does not specify the sensitivity of the data being transmitted via email. - Email notifications for rejections must not contain sensitive PII or full instrument details; they should only contain a reference ID and a link to the secure portal for viewing error details.

OPEN: The PRD mentions an estimated load of 200-500 ISINs per day but does not define peak throughput or concurrency requirements. - The system must support a peak throughput of 50 requests per minute to handle burst trading activity.

OPEN: The PRD requires manual input screens for BCP but does not define the data integrity or validation rules for manual overrides. - Manual ISIN entries must undergo the same validation logic as automated SWIFT requests to ensure data consistency.

OPEN: The system capacity requirements are not defined beyond the daily volume estimate. - The system must support a peak throughput of at least 500 ISIN requests per day, with the ability to handle bursts of 50 requests within a 15-minute window.
